_meta.baton: T1 — make wrong-drug citation visible to the gates (instrument work only)
_meta.constraint_1: ownership only, never mention — see owner_assertion.py docstring
_meta.owner_moieties_note: The corpus key is the TFDA backbone drug_name verbatim (scripts/build_dailymed_label_corpus.py:99-105), so ONE substance can occupy TWO moiety keys with different reference labels and different safety coverage. An owner set that omits a synonym silently flips a RANKING failure into a COVERAGE gap. That is not hypothetical — it is the recorded c1 error (BACKLOG.md:860). Hence owner_moieties is a set, and owner_moieties_alt records the competing reading so neither is chosen silently.
_meta.class_membership_note: owner_moieties lists SYNONYMS OF ONE SUBSTANCE. It is NOT a class-membership list. Class queries are excluded entirely (decision (a)); no class roster appears anywhere in this fixture file.

fixtures.query: aspirin contraindications and who should not take it

owner_moieties_alt.label: c1-adjudication reading (ASPIRIN key only)
owner_moieties_alt.why_recorded: The c1/c2 adjudication resolved aspirin to the ASPIRIN key alone (reference label VAZALORE, OTC, zero whitelisted safety sections) and concluded a COVERAGE gap. Including the synonym key ACETYLSALICYLIC ACID (reference label DURLAZA, Rx, sections 34070-3/34073-7/43685-7) reclassifies it as a RANKING failure. Both readings are reported; the founder decides which is authoritative.

fixtures.synonym_justification: Acetylsalicylic acid IS aspirin — same active substance, not a related drug and not a class sibling.
fixtures.recorded_evidence: aspirin -> ACECLOFENAC cited 12/12 across two index configs, zero variance (docs/c2_phase1c_20260804.md Part 1; BACKLOG.md:894). Treated as N=1 deterministic identity, not 12 independent samples.

owner_moieties_alt.label: salt-inclusive reading (adds IBUPROFEN LYSINE)
owner_moieties_alt.why_recorded: IBUPROFEN resolves to ADVIL (OTC, zero whitelisted safety sections). IBUPROFEN LYSINE resolves to NEOPROFEN (34070-3/34073-7/43685-7) — the same active moiety as a lysine salt, but an INTRAVENOUS NEONATAL product for patent ductus arteriosus closure. Whether NEOPROFEN's warnings legitimately answer an adult oral ibuprofen question is a CLINICAL judgment, not a lexical one.

fixtures.founder_decision_pending: 🔴 FLAG (CLAUDE.md: flag medical ambiguity, do not best-guess). Under the strict reading this fixture is a COVERAGE gap; under the salt-inclusive reading it is a RANKING question. Both are reported. Not decided by this baton.
fixtures.recorded_evidence: ibuprofen warnings -> PIROXICAM, MEFENAMIC ACID, IBUPROFEN LYSINE and (on the E-A index) METHOXSALEN, a psoralen (docs/c2_phase1b_measurement_20260804.md:205, :215).
fixtures.expected_outcome_primary: unset — reported, not asserted, pending the clinical decision above

fixtures.retained_why: Kept in the fixture file deliberately. It is the recorded evidence for BACKLOG surface 3, and the POTASSIUM CHLORIDE #34073-7 label is a legitimate answer despite not being spironolactone-owned. v1 has no non-mention-based way to judge that, so it is reported `unclassified` and NEVER as passing — an instrument that scored a known defect as fine would be a fresh instance of the blindness class it exists to detect.
